about: Forge Cellars was founded on the east side of Seneca Lake by New York winegrower Rick Rainey and Louis Barruol, owner of Château de Saint Cosme in Gigondas, with a first vintage in 2011. Known first for bone-dry Riesling and cool-climate Pinot Noir, the team added Cabernet Franc in 2019, and it has quickly become one of the most talked-about parts of their range, with single-vineyard bottlings from several Seneca Lake sites.

Willow is one of the northernmost vineyards Forge works with on Seneca Lake, a site that also gives the winery a Willow Dry Riesling. The Cabernet Franc is a single-variety wine, handled lightly in the cellar in keeping with Forge’s approach of hand harvesting, spontaneous fermentation with native yeasts and minimal intervention, so the cool northern site and the vintage do the talking.

In the glass this is Cabernet Franc in its fresher, Loire-leaning style: red fruit, savory herbs and fine tannins, with bright acidity. VinePair named the 2023 Willow a value pick with 95 points, praising its precision and savory finish, and Jamie Goode scored the 2021 at 94. It is a natural match for lamb, pork or grilled mushrooms, and takes a light chill well.
